query_text: Given a <span> in HTML I want to change its color on mouse over.

parts.text: The easiest and most efficient way to change the color of a `` on hover is by using **CSS**. You can also do this using **JavaScript** if you need it to trigger dynamic logic. Here are the best ways to do it: --- ### Method 1: Using CSS (Recommended) This is the best practice because it is lightweight, performs better, and doesn't require any JavaScript. You use the `:hover` pseudo-class. **HTML:** ```html Hover over me! ``` **CSS:** ```css .hover-text { color: black; /* Initial color */ cursor: pointer; /* Optional: changes cursor to a hand */ transition: color 0.3s ease; /* Optional: makes the color change smooth */ } .hover-text:hover { color: red; /* Color on hover */ } ``` --- ### Method 2: Inline JavaScript (Quickest for simple tasks) If you cannot edit your external stylesheet and need a quick inline solution, you can use the HTML `onmouseover` and `onmouseout` attributes. **HTML:** ```html Hover over me! ``` --- ### Method 3: JavaScript Event Listeners (Best for dynamic JS apps) If you are writing clean, modern JavaScript and want to separate your HTML from your logic, you can use event listeners. **HTML:** ```html Hover over me! ``` **JavaScript:** ```javascript const span = document.getElementById('dynamic-span'); // Change color on mouse enter span.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => { span.style.color = 'red'; }); // Revert color on mouse leave span.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => { span.style.color = 'black'; }); ``` ### Which one should you choose? * Use **Method 1 (CSS)** for 99% of use cases. It is the cleanest and fastest. * Use **Method 2 or 3 (JavaScript)** only if you need the color change to trigger other JavaScript functions at the same time.
